name: Uni Manager
northStar: A gunmetal rack of buff paper strips, after air traffic control progress boards. Every assessment is a strip seated in a ruled bay; the rack shows your standing without being asked.
rules: Buff is the only large light field, and it always means a real record. Nothing decorative is ever buff.
Every colour channel states exactly one thing: unit hue is identity, lamp colour is urgency. Never emphasis, selection, or delight.
A strip's size is its weighting. Size is data, not layout convenience.
Warn, never silently correct. Where the numbers are ambiguous, say so and keep computing.
A grade band is shown only when nothing is outstanding. Mid-semester the running total is a floor, not a grade.

contrast.verifiedBy: scripts/verify-ui.mjs computes ratios from rendered pixels on every screen
notes: Inks on stock are checked against blank stock (#a79e8b), the darker of the two, because urgency inks only ever land on ungraded strips.
Lamp colours clear 4.5:1 on rack-600, the lightest ground any of them sits on, because they carry text as well as fills.
Unit hues always take rack-900 ink: dark ink clears AA on all eight, white clears it on none.

elevation.philosophy: Almost none. Paper in a metal channel is not floating.
elevation.header: backdrop-filter: blur(4px) — a specific effect for content scrolling under a sticky bar, not decoration
banned: gradients of any kind as surface treatment

motion.philosophy: Transitions carry state change only. Nothing animates on entrance; a rack does not assemble itself.
motion.reducedMotion: All durations collapse to 0.01ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.notes: The assessment rack is a true grid at lg and stacks per-strip below it, each field carrying its own small label. Band scale labels drop their numbers below sm, where four labels between 50 and 80 would collide.

families.sans: Archivo — everything read as language, including the gauge's display figure
families.mono: JetBrains Mono — only where a figure is measured or compared

numerals.default: tabular-nums globally; nearly every figure is compared against one above or below it
numerals.exception: The gauge headline is proportional. There is no column there, and a monospaced decimal point takes a full digit cell, rendering 9.4 as '9 . 4'.

strip.description: A record. Clean stock is graded; hatched blank stock is not yet.

stripPending.description: Blank stock. Sets background-color as well as background-image so dark ink stays readable if the gradient never paints.

rackBay.description: The ruled channel strips are seated in. The 3px seam shows the channel both strips sit in, rather than a gap between two objects.

unitPlate.description: A unit's painted plate. Always shows code or name, so colour is never the only channel carrying identity.

lamp.description: A 6px urgency dot, always paired with text. The only round thing in the system.

buttonPrimary.description: A buff plate: the one thing on the rack you write on.

control.description: An input on the rack face.

cell.description: An always-live editable cell on a strip. No borders until hover; commits on blur or Enter, reverts on Escape.

bayLabel.description: A stencilled section plate over a hairline rule. Never carries an eyebrow above it.

browserSurfaces.selection: lamp-live ground with rack-900 text; inverted to ink-on-stock inside a strip
browserSurfaces.caret: lamp-live on the rack, strip-ink on stock
browserSurfaces.scrollbar: thin, rack-500 thumb on rack-900 track
browserSurfaces.colorScheme: dark; date inputs inside strips are forced light to match the stock

donts: Buff for anything that is not a record
Unit hue for emphasis, or lamp colour for selection
Rounded cards, progress rings, donut charts, gradients
An eyebrow or kicker above a heading
A grade band on a unit with work outstanding
A Unicode glyph where an icon belongs
